property_summary: For any sender and any msg.value, calling addToBalance increases that sender's stored userBalance by exactly msg.value (i.e., newBalance == oldBalance + msg.value); the mutant that doubles msg.value violates this for inputs with msg.value > 0.

For any caller and any nonzero Ether value they send, calling addToBalance increases their recorded userBalance by exactly the sent msg.value; the mutant that adds zero breaks this by leaving userBalance unchanged for some inputs (nonzero value).

For any caller and any nonzero sent value, after calling addToBalance with that value the contract's recorded userBalance for that caller increases by at least the sent value (i.e., new balance >= previous balance + sent value); the mutant that ignores msg.value breaks this because balances do not increase when msg.value>0.

After any successful addToBalance() call by a user, that user's recorded balance in the correct contract remains equal to the amount they sent (no unexpected decrease via reentrancy); the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during its addToBalance call and thus makes the final stored balance differ.

For any caller and any deposit amount > 0, after caller calls addToBalance sending that amount, the contract's recorded userBalance for that caller equals the prior balance plus the sent amount in the correct C; the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to disturb balances during addToBalance so this equality can be violated for some inputs.

For any depositor address and deposit amount > 0, when that depositor calls addToBalance (payable), the contract's total ETH balance increases by exactly that amount (no external reentrant withdrawal can reduce c's balance during the deposit) — the mutant that skips setting locked_ = true permits reentrancy during deposit and can cause c.address.balance to be lower than expected for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount > 0 made through an externally-owned account that is ALSO a contract capable of reentering (attacker contract), the correct C never observes a change in that depositor's recorded userBalance during the execution of addToBalance (i.e., no reentrant withdrawal can run during addToBalance), whereas the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true permits reentrancy so the recorded balance after addToBalance can be smaller than expected for some attacker addresses and amounts.

For any depositor address and amount, when a (possibly malicious) contract calls addToBalance sending that amount, the correct contract C never allows reentrant withdrawals during addToBalance so the depositor's recorded userBalance after the call equals prior balance + amount; the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during addToBalance and thus can make the final recorded userBalance differ for some attacker contract and amount.

Invariant: after any successful withdrawBalance() call by a user, that user's stored balance in C is zero (reference preserves zeroing after external call); the buggy mutant that zeroes before sending can leave the recorded balance non-zero when reentrancy occurs, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any user and deposit amount, if a user calls withdrawBalance() then after the call completes the contract's stored user balance for that caller is zero; the mutant that zeros before making the external call can be re-entered by a malicious recipient and leave the stored balance non-zero, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any attacker address and deposited amount, if the attacker deposits then calls withdrawBalance() (where the recipient can reenter), the reference contract always ends with getBalance(attacker) == 0 after withdraw completes; the mutant that zeroes before the external call can be reentered and leave a non-zero stored balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and any attacker helper contract that reenters on receive, if the depositor funds the contract and then calls withdrawBalance(), the reference C will always finish with address(c).balance == 0 (all funds sent out) for every admissible input; the mutant that zeros early can be re-entered and leave ether stuck in C, so address(c).balance > 0 for some inputs.

For any depositor and any attacker contract that re-enters on receive, when the attacker deposits some nonzero amount then calls withdrawBalance(), the reference C always finishes with the attacker's recorded userBalance equal to 0 (no balance left) after withdraw returns; the mutant that zeroes before the external call can be re-entered and cause the stored balance to remain >0, violating this rule for some inputs.

After a successful withdrawBalance call by any user, the contract's userBalance for that user is zero in the correct version; the mutant that fails to reset the reentrancy lock can cause withdrawBalance to revert on subsequent interactions (or leave the balance non-zero), so there exist inputs (an attacker that reverts on call) that make the mutant violate this invariant.

After a user funds the contract and then calls withdrawBalance, the reference contract always leaves every other user's balance unchanged (withdraw only affects the caller's balance); the mutant that zeroes the caller's balance after sending can be re-entered to alter other users' balances, breaking this invariant for some inputs.
